contests.title: Geneva Joint No. 4 School District — Temporary school-revenue increase

provenance.quote: BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of Geneva Joint 4 School District, Walworth County, Wisconsin, that the revenues included in the Geneva Joint 4 School District budget be authorized to exceed the revenue limit specified in Section 121.91(2m), Wisconsin Statutes, by $750,000 in the 2027-2028 school year, by $1,000,000 in the 2028-2029 school year, by $1,250,000 in the 2029-2030 school year, and by $1,500,000 in the 2030-2031 school year for non-recurring purposes of paying the ongoing operational expenses of the school district. Adopted and Recorded August 19,2026.

contests.title: Glenwood City School District — Temporary school-revenue increase

provenance.quote:
RESOLUTION PROVIDING FOR A REFERENDUM ELECTION ON THE QUESTION OF THE APPROVAL OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE SCHOOL DISTRICT BUDGET TO EXCEED REVENUE LIMIT BY $750,000 PER YEAR FOR FOUR YEARS FOR NON-RECURRING PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the School Board of the School District of Glenwood City, St. Croix and Dunn Counties, Wisconsin (the "District"), has heretofore duly adopted a resolution entitled: "Resolution Authorizing the School District Budget to Exceed Revenue Limit by $750,000 Per Year for Four Years for Non-Recurring Purposes" (the "Revenue Limit Resolution"); and WHEREAS, the School Board deems it to be desirable and in the best interest of the District to direct the District Clerk to submit the Revenue Limit Resolution to the electors for approval or rejection at the regularly scheduled election to be held on November 3, 2026.

contests.title: Hillsboro School District — Temporary school-revenue increase

provenance.quote: BE IT RESOLVED by the School Board of the School District of Hillsboro, Vernon, Richland, Monroe, Juneau and Sauk Counties, Wisconsin that the revenues included in the School District budget be authorized to exceed the revenue limit specified in  Section 121.91, Wisconsin Statutes, by $1,100,000 per year for four years, beginning with the 2027-2028 school year and ending with the 2030-2031 school year, for non-recurring purposes to maintain District facilities and current programs.

contests.title: Marinette School District — School improvement bonds

provenance.quote:
General obligation bonds in an amount not to exceed $68,000,000 for the public purpose of
paying the cost of a school facility improvement project at the Middle and High Schools
consisting of: construction of additions and renovations at the Middle School, including for
career and technical education, art, music, special education and commons spaces; renovations at
the High School, including to career and technical education, music, science spaces and locker
rooms; building infrastructure, systems, safety, security, accessibility and site improvements; and

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows the district to raise money above Wisconsin’s school-revenue limit for four school years: $750,000 in 2027–28, $1 million in 2028–29, $1.25 million in 2029–30, and $1.5 million in 2030–31. It would pay for the school district’s ongoing operations. This temporary authorization ends after those years.

Allows the district to raise $750,000 a year above Wisconsin’s school-revenue limit for four school years, from 2026–27 through 2029–30, for operations and maintenance. This temporary authorization ends after those years.

Allows the district to raise $1.1 million a year above Wisconsin’s school-revenue limit for four school years, from 2027–28 through 2030–31, to maintain district facilities and current programs. This temporary authorization ends after those years.

Allows the district to borrow up to $68 million through general obligation bonds for improvements at the middle and high schools. These include middle-school additions and renovations for career and technical education, art, music, special education and common spaces; high-school renovations for career and technical education, music, science and locker rooms; infrastructure, building systems, safety, security, accessibility and school-site work; and furnishings, fixtures and equipment.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve borrowing up to $68 million for these projects.
